Don't chase Monday's open; wait for either capitulation low or VIX cooling below 16.

trade_setups.thesis: Semis ETF broke decisively below 50DMA; NVDA/AMD/AVGO led downside -3 to -6%. AI capex narrative cracked for first time in months. Momentum unwind has room to run if VIX stays above 18.

Only S&P sector green today (+2.36%) driven by WTI breaking $100. If oil holds above $98, energy is the rare risk-on hide-out: inflation-hedge profile, FCF strong at this oil deck, sector neglected for months.
Russell 2000 led the downside -2.44%; small caps lack the mega-cap defensive bid and have the most domestic-economy sensitivity to rising long yields. Cleanest expression of breadth-breakdown thesis.

bear_case: Counter-argument: today's action may reflect Friday options-expiry mechanics plus delta hedging rather than a true regime change. Friday OPEX historically produces sharp moves that reverse on Monday. VIX at 18.43 is elevated but well below panic territory (>25). The dollar barely moved (DXY -0.01%) — a genuine macro break would typically pair with a flight-to-USD bid. The oil spike may prove to be a one-off geopolitical premium already absorbed in the price rather than persistent inflation pressure. Invalidation level: if SPX reclaims 7,460 by midday Monday with VIX printing below 17, the step-aside call is wrong and the right adjustment is back to selective BUY by Tuesday's open.
